WITH first_terms AS (
    SELECT
        id_bioguide,
        MIN(term_start) AS first_term_start
    FROM city_legislation.main.legislators_terms
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
    HAVING MIN(term_start) B

content.text: I will now construct the query to calculate the legislator retention rate. First, I will identify the cohort of legislators whose first term began between 1917 and 1999. Next, I will generate a series of 20 subsequent years to check for retention. I will then determine which legislators from the initial cohort were still in office at the end of each of those 20 years. Finally, I will calculate the retention rate for each year by dividing the number of retained legislators by the total size of the initial cohort.

args.sql:
WITH first_terms AS (
    SELECT
        id_bioguide,
        MIN(term_start) AS first_term_start
    FROM city_legislation.main.legislators_terms
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
    HAVING MIN(term_start) BETWEEN '1917-01-01' AND '1999-12-31'
),
years_of_service AS (
    SELECT CAST(range AS INT) AS year_of_service
    FROM range(1, 21)
),
cohort_retention AS (
    SELECT
        ft.id_bioguide,
        ys.year_of_service,
        ft.first_term_start,
        MAX(CASE 
            WHEN DATE_TRUNC('year', ft.first_term_start::DATE) + INTERVAL '1 year' * ys.year_of_service + INTERVAL '11 month' + INTERVAL '30 day' BETWEEN lt.term_start::DATE AND lt.term_end::DATE THEN 1
            ELSE 0 
        END) AS retained
    FROM first_terms ft
    CROSS JOIN years_of_service ys
    LEFT JOIN city_legislation.main.legislators_terms lt ON ft.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    GROUP BY ft.id_bioguide, ys.year_of_service, ft.first_term_start
)
SELECT
    cr.year_of_service,
    100 * SUM(cr.retained) / COUNT(DISTINCT cr.id_bioguide) AS retention_rate
FROM cohort_retention cr
GROUP BY cr.year_of_service
ORDER BY cr.year_of_service;
